messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Compiling error when running the stan analyses in Rstan on windows 7
parts:
On Wednesday, June 1, 2016 at 12:13:59 PM UTC-4, Yang Hu wrote:

ERROR(s) during compilation: source code errors or compiler configuration errors!

    Other relevant information are listed as follows:
> sessionInfo()
R version 3.3.0 (2016-05-03)
R >= 3.3.0 does not work with ...

> system("g++ --version") 
G__~1.EXE (GCC) 4.6.3 20111208 (prerelease)

To use R >= 3.3.0 you need g++ 4.9.x from Rtools33. There are some details at

https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/wiki/RStan-Getting-Started

but basically it boils down to getting R:\Rtools\mingw_64\bin on the PATH.

Ben

    I was wondering: if I use an older version of R and Rtool, do you think it will change something?

and then try to compile a Stan model.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Compiling error when running the stan analyses in Rstan on windows 7
parts:
On Thursday, June 2, 2016 at 7:13:48 AM UTC-4, Yang Hu wrote:
Another update: I tried in a desktop with win7 64-bit OS, it worked (for the "8 schools" example). So it is probably because of the RAM problem (I guess).

It is difficult to use Stan productively on a 32bit OS that can only access 4GB of address space. But the 8 schools example shouldn't require that much, presuming you can get it to compile. So, I would guess that it is a configuration problem on your laptop but even if you overcame that, it might not be so feasible to use that laptop for actual research with Stan.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Compiling error when running the stan analyses in Rstan on windows 7

On Thursday, June 2, 2016 at 11:36:04 AM UTC-4, Daniel Lee wrote:
Isn't there a binary install for RStan on Windows 32-bit? The stanc compiler requires high memory to build. Most Stan programs take less, I think, until you start building models on matrices.

There is a binary install but mingw's g++-4.9 consumes more memory compiling than 4.6 did, so the range of models that can be compiled on a 32bit OS is smaller.

Ben
